text: That radiation to the jaw and arm with exertion is very concerning for cardiac ischemia. Have you noticed any associated symptoms like nausea, lightheadedness, or palpitations during these episodes? Also, do you have a history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol?

text: Given the normal troponin and ECG findings showing only ischemia without infarction, have you noticed any swelling in your legs or shortness of breath when lying flat? Also, do you experience sudden shortness of breath or coughing up pink, frothy sputum?

text: Thank you for clarifying; the absence of heart failure symptoms helps narrow the focus. Given your significant smoking history and exertional chest pain, have you noticed any burning sensation in your chest that improves with antacids, or any difficulty swallowing? REQUEST TEST: Lipid Panel

text: The lipid panel confirms significant dyslipidemia, which combined with your hypertension and smoking history strongly supports a diagnosis of stable angina due to coronary artery disease.
